title: Anchored Context: playpad for persistent mini-objects
body:
Brain dump / rough PRD sketch for 'Anchored Context' feature — small, user-definable context objects that live outside the volatile turn history and can be referenced or merged into prompts with low token overhead. Goal: give product teams predictable, reusable micro-contexts (facts, personas, short tool outputs) that reduce repeated prompting and improve quality while saving tokens.

Problem statement / motivating examples:
- Chatbots keep re-sending the same 200-token instructions (company policy, user profile snippet) every session. Wasteful for cost and brittle for updates.
- User-facing assistants need stable facts (account tier, phone number formatting, canned legal phrasing) that should persist across sessions and be editable independent of message history.
- Some customers want deterministic persona anchors (tone = "concise, legal") applied across many conversations without injecting long prompt blocks each time.

High level idea:
- Anchors = small named objects (max N bytes/tokens) stored on user/customer scope (customer-level or session-scope) in Redwood storage layer.
- Anchors can be referenced by name in templates, or automatically merged by server-side policies before generation.
- Support three modes: inline-merge (tokens are appended), compositional-embed (anchor stored as embedding and used in reranking/recall), and policy-apply (runtime rules include/exclude anchors based on triggers).

User stories:
- As a product engineer, I want to create a 'support-guidelines' anchor so every support assistant call automatically gets the latest policy without adding tokens to my prompts manually.
- As an admin, I want to edit the 'brand-voice' anchor and have changes take effect immediately in conversations without redeploying prompts.
- As an SRE, I want anchors to be small and fast to fetch (cached TTLs) so we don't add latency to generation paths.

Acceptance criteria (rough):
- API: create/list/get/delete anchors on customer and session scope. Anchor metadata includes name, type (text/json), version, last_modified, size_bytes.
- Runtime: merging an anchor into a generation flow should add <= anchor_size tokens; fetching anchor from store + cache add <= 15ms p99 on hosted infra.
- UX: console page to create and preview anchors; a simple test harness to simulate apply rules and show token delta.
- Observability: per-anchor usage metrics (applies, avg token delta, failures), audit trail for edits, and rollback to previous versions.

API sketch (very rough):
- POST /v1/customers/{c}/anchors -> {name, scope, content, mode, tags} -> returns anchor_id
- GET /v1/customers/{c}/anchors -> list
- GET /v1/customers/{c}/anchors/{name} -> {content, version, last_modified}
- POST /v1/sessions/{s}/apply -> {prompt, anchors: ["support-guidelines"], rules: {on_error: fallback}} -> returns merged_prompt + chosen_anchor_versions
- Webhook for anchor-update events so private deployments can invalidate caches.

UX flows / console notes:
- Anchor editor: small textarea or JSON editor + preview panel that shows tokenized representation and estimated token/latency cost.
- Permissioning: anchor create/edit reserved to org-admins or roles; read for service accounts.
- Preview tester: simulate a chat request and show before/after tokens and a diff of model output with/without anchor.

Rollout plan ideas:
- Phase 0: internal alpha for Redwood support/chatbots only (limit per-customer active anchors to 5).
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for Hosted API customers with feature flag; add console page and API.
- Phase 2: expose per-route automatic anchor policies (route-level config in Console).
- Phase 3: Dedicated/Private support with configurable storage (customer-managed store) and audit HSM/KMS integration for sensitive anchors.

Metrics to watch:
- token_saved_per_request (est) aggregated by anchor; % requests using anchors; p50/p95 fetch latency; anchor_edit_rate; downstream quality deltas (BLEU-ish / custom eval) per anchor change.

Open implementation questions / risks:
- How to version anchors safely when rolling forward/backward? Need immutable versions and server-side referential semantics.
- Security: anchors may contain PII or customer secrets. Options: encrypt-at-rest with KMS, limit content size, or disallow certain fields.
- Cache invalidation: updates must appear within Xs for support use-cases — tradeoff between hot caches and freshness.
- How to minimize token delta: could use short canonical keys + server-side templating rather than raw content injection. But templating complexity rises.
- Multi-model semantics: some anchors should be model-agnostic (rules only), others are model-specific (templated prompts adjusted per model).

Experiment ideas / quick tests:
- A/B test: support bot responses with anchor vs duplicated prompt text across 100k sessions; measure token cost delta and satisfaction score.
- Quick proto: implement anchors as small key-value store + server-side merge in a Lambda for one customer (no console) to validate token/latency tradeoffs.
- Embedding experiment: store anchor as embedding and score it as additional context in retrieval-augmented flow instead of token injection. Compare quality.

Implementation sketch (infra):
- Storage: small KV with versioning; metadata in main DB; large-anchor guard rails (max 2KB).
- CDN-like caches in serving runtime keyed by customer + anchor-version; eviction TTL config per-customer.
- Authorization: ties to API keys / org perms. Add audit log table for edits.

Notes / todo (actionable):
- [ ] Spike: simple server-side merge prototype using hosted API (target 2 dev days). Owner: Brielle/Evan.
- [ ] Design console editor wireframe (product). Owner: Maya.
- [ ] Security review for PII handling; propose KMS envelope. Owner: Kai.
- [ ] Add telemetry events to runtime for 'anchor.apply' with token_delta. Owner: infra team.

Questions for discussion in sync:
- default scope: should anchors be customer-level by default or per-route?
- lifetime: do we want an expiration TTL on anchors? useful for ephemeral contexts (promos).
- ergonomics: template language vs raw text insertion — how powerful do we make it?

Related notes/links (placeholders):
- quick idea: combine anchors with session-presets so users can opt into anchor bundles (e.g., enterprise-onboarding-bundle).
- cross-ref: conversation-anchors vs progressive-semantic-anchors doc — need to reconcile (this feature focuses on named, small, editable objects rather than large semantic caches).

Rough copy for console blurb:
"Anchors are small persistent context objects you can attach to routes or sessions. Use anchors for stable facts, brand voice snippets, or short policy text. Anchors are versioned, editable, and designed to reduce repeated prompt tokens while keeping your assistant consistent."

End-of-playpad. Random notes: keep anchor size small, support both inline and embedding patterns, provide clear audit trail. Will iterate after spike.
